page: Microsoft Azure E2as_v6 is a memory-optimized instance belonging to the Eav6 family, deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine is driven by an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz, providing 2 vCPUs backed by 1 dedicated physical core and 2 threads. Cache hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 16.0 GB, establishing a high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread compute capabilities, with stress-ng single-core output reaching 3078.58 and Geekbench single-core scoring 1961.0, both placing in the top quartile of assessed systems. In contrast, aggregate multi-core throughput is constrained by the two-thread ceiling, resulting in lower-quartile placements for multi-core stress-ng, multi-core Geekbench (2421.0), and PassMark CPU (3834.16). Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 37.22 GB/sec, while write bandwidth reaches an average 27.74 GB/sec. Application-level metrics reflect these limits, showing 2.91 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.41 GB/sec of static web throughput.

Because the E2as_v6 allocates an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio on dedicated AMD silicon, it delivers cost-effective RAM density for applications that demand capacity over raw compute parallelization. The trade-off lies in multi-threaded execution and storage, as workloads needing significant local disk input/output must utilize remote storage options. The configuration is primarily matched for small in-memory key-value databases, lightweight caching tiers, microservices with high working-set footprints, and low-concurrency batch processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E2as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz across 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core. The system provisions 16.0 GB of memory, equating to an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache, with no integrated local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark profiles highlight strong single-core performance, achieving top-quartile results in Geekbench single-core and stress-ng tests, while multi-core metrics remain lower due to the 2-vCPU hardware allocation. Memory bandwidth registers at 27.74 GB/sec for uncached writes and 37.22 GB/sec for uncached reads. Delivering high memory density relative to core count, the E2as_v6 provides a balanced platform for lightweight in-memory databases, caching nodes, and memory-bound backend microservices with modest thread concurrency requirements.
